QF.id: XIII Introduction to Forwards and Futures_62

question.text: Using the interest-rate-parity approximation, what is the theoretical 3-month USDINR forward premium if the Indian rate is 6.5% and the US rate is 4%?

answer.text: Approximately 0.625% for 3 months or 2.5% annualised [(6.5% − 4%) × 3/12 = 0.625% for 3 months; annualised differential = 2.5%]

explanation.text: The Logic: Series I (pp.63-64) gives the forward premium as the interest-rate differential under interest-rate parity. Annualised differential = 6.5% − 4% = 2.5%; pro-rated to 3 months: 2.5% × 3/12 = 0.625%. The exact form is F = S × (1.065^0.25)/(1.04^0.25), but the simple-interest approximation is close. The Trap: 10.5% adds the two rates instead of subtracting. "2.5% for 3 months" fails to pro-rate the annualised differential. 0.15% is too low. The previously printed "2.40% annualised" figure was internally inconsistent with the 0.625% three-month value. Note: Source-backed by Series I Currency Derivatives workbook, pages 63-64.
